claim.pdf_says: BLOCK CONTAINS [integer-1 TO] integer-2 {RECORDS / CHARACTERS} (RECORDS underlined; CHARACTERS printed without underline)
claim.why_it_matters: Same added underline in the relative-file FD (V-10): CHARACTERS is an optional word in the printed figure (§1985:IV.2.1.2), the markdown marks it a required key word, so BLOCK CONTAINS integer-2 with CHARACTERS omitted reads as illegal.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered page 202 (V-10, relative-file FD general format) at 300 dpi. In the BLOCK CONTAINS clause the brace stacks RECORDS over CHARACTERS: RECORDS carries an underline, CHARACTERS has none (compare the underlined BLOCK and TO on the same line). page-202.md line 22 writes <u>CHARACTERS</u>, which adds an underline the printed figure does not have. In 1985 notation an un-underlined word is optional, so in this brace (exactly one option, explicitly specified or implicitly selected) CHARACTERS may be omitted. The transcription makes it a required key word. That changes the syntax, so it is normative. The RECORD CONTAINS lines correctly leave CHARACTERS un-underlined, which confirms the BLOCK line is the error.
